customer_name: China Southern Power Grid Guangdong Customer Service Center (广东电网客服中心)
business_problem: Guangdong's power-customer service operation needed a more intelligent service backbone for its 24x7 hotline and digital channels so it could improve intent understanding, reduce handling time, and give agents better answers at large scale.
solution_summary: Baidu AI Cloud privately deployed a full intelligent-customer-service stack for China Southern Power Grid's Guangdong customer-service center. The project started from scratch with intelligent text service, rebuilt the hotline IVR experience, and added a unified knowledge base so service logic and answers could be reused across channels. At the model layer, Baidu combined intent recognition, entity extraction, multi-turn dialogue, and semantic understanding with Guangdong Grid's own industry customer-service data to fine-tune a power-domain large model. The resulting platform serves both self-service users and human agents: online customers can resolve common requests automatically, while agents receive answer suggestions and structured knowledge support through the same shared service backbone. By combining private deployment, domain data, and self-learning knowledge management, the platform turned a traditional power contact center into an AI-assisted service operation with measurable improvements in resolution and productivity.

solution_components.name: Intelligent Customer Service
solution_components.role: Delivers automated text-based customer support across Guangdong Grid's service channels.

solution_components.name: Intelligent IVR
solution_components.role: Modernizes the hotline's voice-service flow with AI-driven interaction and routing.

solution_components.name: Unified Intelligent Knowledge Base
solution_components.role: Provides the shared answer corpus used by bots and agents and improves itself from historical conversations.

solution_components.name: Power Customer Service Large Model
solution_components.role: Applies intent recognition, entity recognition, multi-turn dialogue, and semantic understanding to power-sector service questions.

data_flow: Customer requests from online text channels and the 95598 hotline enter the shared intelligent-service layer. The large model classifies intent and entities, the knowledge base returns grounded answers or agent suggestions, and both self-service and human-assisted flows feed conversation history back into the system to strengthen future responses.
business_outcome: Guangdong Grid improved self-service resolution, shortened handling time, boosted seat productivity, and established a reusable AI customer-service foundation for the energy sector.
metrics: The online intelligent service handles 400,000 customers per month on average.
The system covers 1,200 Q&A knowledge items across 36 business scenarios.
architecture_clues: The customer-service stack was privately deployed for the utility rather than delivered as a generic public service.
A single knowledge base supports both automated text service and hotline IVR transformation.
Historical conversations are mined continuously so the knowledge base can self-learn and improve.
